distractor_1: Adopt a rolling release model where each team merges into main daily, using feature flags to hide incomplete work from production queries until fully tested.
explanation_why_it_is_incorrect_1: Daily mainline merges risk introducing unreviewed changes. The better approach is to develop in separate branches with peer review before integration, which provides stronger quality control.

distractor_1: Configure the prod target in dbt for both automated deployments and analyst experiments to ensure datasets match across testing and live usage scenarios.
explanation_why_it_is_incorrect_1: Using the production target for experiments risks altering live data. A safer practice is to work in a dedicated development target and reserve production for finalized deployments.

distractor_1: Schedule quarterly branch merges where all new features are integrated at once, conducting code reviews after the combined branch passes system-wide regression tests.
explanation_why_it_is_incorrect_1: Reviewing only after a large merge can delay detection of issues. Reviewing each feature branch before merging catches problems earlier and reduces the scope of integration conflicts.

distractor_1: Permit small hotfixes to bypass branch creation and be applied directly to production during off-hours, documenting the change afterward in commit messages.
explanation_why_it_is_incorrect_1: Bypassing branch review for hotfixes can introduce hidden bugs. Even urgent fixes benefit from branch-based workflows with quick peer review before going live.

distractor_1: Design a workflow where developers test locally on the production schema to avoid discrepancies, switching to development targets only for destructive schema changes.
explanation_why_it_is_incorrect_1: Running tests on the production schema risks unintended changes to live data. Using a development schema for local work keeps production stable while still allowing accurate testing.

distractor_1: Implement trunk-based development with automated quality gates, letting passing code flow straight to production without manual branch management.
explanation_why_it_is_incorrect_1: Automation improves speed but cannot replace human review. Branch-based development with peer review adds a safeguard against logic errors that automated checks might miss.

distractor_1: Create multiple dev targets in the same profile, but configure all deployments — including experimental builds — to run through the prod target for consistency.
explanation_why_it_is_incorrect_1: Running experiments through the production target risks introducing incomplete features to live data. Development targets isolate work-in-progress from production workloads.

distractor_1: Allow merging of branches into production once they pass automated linting and unit tests, deferring human review until post-deployment retrospectives.
explanation_why_it_is_incorrect_1: Automated checks can’t catch every issue. Pre-merge peer review is more effective because it can identify logic flaws or unintended impacts before changes reach production.

distractor_1: Store API keys and database passwords directly in configuration files within the repository to ensure all team members have consistent access credentials.
explanation_why_it_is_incorrect_1: Storing secrets in repositories creates security vulnerabilities and version control history exposure. Use environment variables or secret management systems to keep credentials secure.

distractor_1: Configure Kubernetes pods to run as root user by default to avoid permission issues when accessing system resources and mounting volumes.
explanation_why_it_is_incorrect_1: Running containers as root violates the principle of least privilege and increases security risks. Use non-root users and configure appropriate permissions through security contexts.

distractor_1: Implement database migrations by directly executing ALTER TABLE statements in production during peak hours to ensure immediate schema updates.
explanation_why_it_is_incorrect_1: Running migrations during peak hours can cause downtime and lock contentions. Schedule migrations during maintenance windows and use techniques like blue-green deployments for zero-downtime updates.

distractor_1: Use SELECT * in production SQL queries to automatically include new columns as the schema evolves, reducing maintenance overhead.
explanation_why_it_is_incorrect_1: SELECT * queries can break applications when schemas change and cause performance issues by retrieving unnecessary data. Explicitly specify required columns for better maintainability and performance.

distractor_1: Configure Redis cache with no expiration times to maximize hit rates and avoid cache misses during high-traffic periods.
explanation_why_it_is_incorrect_1: Caches without expiration can grow indefinitely and serve stale data. Set appropriate TTL values based on data freshness requirements and implement cache invalidation strategies.

distractor_1: Deploy microservices updates by stopping all instances simultaneously to ensure version consistency across the entire system.
explanation_why_it_is_incorrect_1: Stopping all instances causes service downtime. Use rolling deployments or blue-green strategies to maintain availability while updating services incrementally.

distractor_1: Store user session data in local server memory to improve response times and reduce external dependencies on session stores.
explanation_why_it_is_incorrect_1: Local session storage doesn't scale across multiple server instances and causes data loss during server restarts. Use distributed session stores like Redis for scalability and persistence.

distractor_1: Configure load balancers to always route requests to the same server based on client IP to maintain session affinity and reduce latency.
explanation_why_it_is_incorrect_1: Sticky sessions based on IP can create uneven load distribution and single points of failure. Use stateless application design with shared session storage for better scalability.

distractor_1: Implement retry logic with immediate retries and no backoff delay to quickly recover from transient failures in distributed systems.
explanation_why_it_is_incorrect_1: Immediate retries without backoff can overwhelm failing services and worsen outages. Use exponential backoff with jitter to avoid thundering herd problems.

distractor_1: Store application logs directly in the database alongside business data to maintain referential integrity and simplify querying.
explanation_why_it_is_incorrect_1: Storing logs in the application database can impact performance and scalability. Use dedicated logging systems like ELK stack or cloud logging services for better separation of concerns.

distractor_1: Configure CI/CD pipelines to deploy directly to production on every commit to the main branch to minimize deployment delays.
explanation_why_it_is_incorrect_1: Automatic production deployment without staging and validation increases risk of deploying broken code. Include staging environments and manual approval gates for production deployments.

distractor_1: Use database transactions sparingly to improve performance, committing changes immediately after each operation.
explanation_why_it_is_incorrect_1: Avoiding transactions can lead to data inconsistency and race conditions. Use appropriate transaction boundaries to maintain ACID properties while balancing performance concerns.

distractor_1: Configure Docker containers to share the host network namespace to eliminate networking overhead and improve communication speed.
explanation_why_it_is_incorrect_1: Sharing host network reduces isolation and can cause port conflicts. Use Docker networking features like bridge networks to maintain isolation while enabling efficient communication.

distractor_1: Implement error handling by catching all exceptions globally and returning generic error messages to avoid exposing system internals.
explanation_why_it_is_incorrect_1: Generic error messages make debugging difficult and provide poor user experience. Implement specific error handling with appropriate logging while sanitizing sensitive information in user-facing messages.

distractor_1: Store application state in global variables across modules to enable easy data sharing between different components.
explanation_why_it_is_incorrect_1: Global state makes applications harder to test, debug, and maintain. Use dependency injection or state management patterns to control data flow and maintain modularity.

distractor_1: Configure autoscaling to scale up aggressively at the first sign of increased load to prevent any performance degradation.
explanation_why_it_is_incorrect_1: Aggressive autoscaling can lead to resource waste and cost overruns. Configure scaling policies with appropriate thresholds and cooldown periods to balance performance and cost efficiency.

distractor_1: Use hardcoded connection strings in application code to ensure consistent database connectivity across all deployment environments.
explanation_why_it_is_incorrect_1: Hardcoded connection strings make applications inflexible and expose credentials in source code. Use configuration management and environment-specific settings for deployment flexibility.

distractor_1: Implement GraphQL resolvers that make individual database queries for each field to maintain clean separation of concerns.
explanation_why_it_is_incorrect_1: Individual queries for each field can cause N+1 query problems and performance issues. Use DataLoader patterns or batch queries to optimize database access in GraphQL resolvers.

distractor_1: Configure monitoring alerts to trigger immediately when any metric deviates from normal values to ensure rapid incident response.
explanation_why_it_is_incorrect_1: Immediate alerts on any deviation can cause alert fatigue and false positives. Set appropriate thresholds and use statistical analysis to reduce noise and focus on actionable alerts.

distractor_1: Store sensitive user data in browser localStorage for quick access and offline functionality without additional security measures.
explanation_why_it_is_incorrect_1: localStorage is accessible to any script and persists data unencrypted. Use secure, httpOnly cookies or encrypted storage for sensitive data, and implement proper data protection measures.
